- Training opt-out workflow: engineering can support a per-project opt-out flag (metadata tag) but need clarity on enforcement: Helio wants to provide a list — do we accept retroactive requests or only prospective flags? Recommended: accept prospective opt-out only (i.e., flags provided before data enters Redwood systems) and retain right to use aggregated metrics. We should state turnaround time (48–72 hours) for flag activation and include operational SLA in Exhibit A.

- MAP: I’ll draft a 1‑page mutual action plan with target sign date and a list of evidence Helio needs. Also linking compliance artifacts (SOC2 report) will be handled by Security; Priyom can advise.

Can you each weigh in on legal language we can present live at 3:30? I’ll keep the call to 30 minutes — objective: land high-level positions so I can tell Helio we have agreement in principle.

Thanks Ben — quick legal positions and suggested edit snippets below (I’ll attach an official redline if we agree): 

1) Product Title / Output Attribution: recommend this language for Exhibit A: "Customer retains title to Customer Materials and any Output that reproduces or is substantially derived from Customer Materials as identified in Exhibit A. For Outputs generated solely from Customer prompts and Redwood models, Customer receives a non-exclusive, non-transferable right to use such Outputs internally and for Customer's productization within its organization; Redwood retains the right to use aggregated, de-identified Outputs for service improvements." 

Rationale: gives Helio the operational assurance they want while preserving Redwood’s right to operate and improve models. We should avoid words like "assignment" which imply exclusive transfer.

2) Training / Feedback License: propose a two-tier approach: (a) Prospective Opt-Out: Customer may provide a list of projects or dataset identifiers to be excluded from training; Redwood will honor flags that are received prior to ingestion. (b) Retroactive Requests: we can accept retroactive deletion requests for specific records on a case-by-case basis subject to technical feasibility and a small operations fee. Add SLA: flag processing within 72 hours, deletion requests acknowledged same-day and completed within 15 business days where feasible.

3) Implementation & Evidence: confirm SOC2 Type II attestation and provide our encryption-at-rest doc. Priyom — can you prepare the SOC2 redaction bundle and a short note on technical enforcement of opt-outs for the call? Marissa — any commercial concessions tied to opt-out tolerance (e.g., reduced unit pricing if Helio blocks telemetry for model improvement) we should consider?

I’ll prepare suggested redline snippets and upload them to the shared Drive.
